items.Criterion: Each recommendation in the DMAIC report includes an estimated scrap reduction.
items.Rationale: The prompt explicitly requires recommendations to include estimated scrap reduction figures.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Recommendations must be data-backed and include estimated scrap reduction and implementation cost or resource estimate'

items.Criterion: Each recommendation in the DMAIC report includes an implementation cost or resource estimate.
items.Rationale: The prompt explicitly requires recommendations to include implementation cost or resource estimates.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Recommendations must be data-backed and include estimated scrap reduction and implementation cost or resource estimate'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report states the current defect or scrap rate as 40%.
items.Rationale: The prompt explicitly states the defect/scrap rate is 40% over the past 3 months; the report must reference this baseline to establish scope.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'There has been a 40% defect/scrap rate for the past 3 months'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report states a target of reducing defects by 20% over the next quarter.
items.Rationale: The prompt explicitly states the goal of a 20% reduction over the next quarter; the report must reflect this target.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'reduce by 20% over the next quarter'

items.Criterion: The Define phase includes a problem statement that references the 40% defect or scrap rate.
items.Rationale: DMAIC best practice requires the Define phase to contain a clear problem statement that quantifies the current-state defect rate. A Define section that omits the baseline metric is incomplete.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Define phase standard content

items.Criterion: The Define phase identifies the project scope as an electronics manufacturing assembly plant.
items.Rationale: DMAIC best practice requires the Define phase to scope the improvement effort. The report should reflect the plant context stated in the prompt.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'electronics manufacturing assembly plant'

items.Criterion: The Measure phase references or summarizes data from the 3-month period.
items.Rationale: DMAIC Measure phase must ground the baseline in quantitative data over the period under review. The report should demonstrate that 3 months of defect data was considered.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'pareto analysis of the previous 3 months' and 'defect_log_3months.xlsx'

items.Criterion: The Measure phase includes or references a Pareto analysis of defect types.
items.Rationale: The prompt provides Pareto analysis data as input; DMAIC Measure/Analyze phases must incorporate this data to establish defect frequency distribution.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'pareto analysis of the previous 3 months in a file called 3mos_pareto.pptx'

items.Criterion: The Analyze phase includes at least one structured root cause analysis technique (such as fishbone, 5 Whys, or fault tree).
items.Rationale: DMAIC Analyze phase requires a formal root cause analysis methodology. Listing causes without an analytical framework does not meet professional DMAIC standards.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Analyze phase standard content

items.Criterion: Each of the 5 identified root causes is linked to at least one supporting data point or evidence from the available defect data.
items.Rationale: The prompt requires recommendations to be data-backed; this same standard applies to root causes identified in the Analyze phase.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Recommendations must be data-backed'

items.Criterion: The root causes identified span at least two distinct manufacturing process categories (such as materials, machine, method, man, or environment).
items.Rationale: A professionally credible root cause analysis for a 40% defect rate in electronics manufacturing must consider multiple cause categories; single-category root cause lists indicate incomplete analysis.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: 5M+1E framework for manufacturing root cause analysis

items.Criterion: The Improve phase contains the 90-day action plan.
items.Rationale: In DMAIC, implementation actions and improvement plans belong in the Improve phase. Placing the action plan in a different section indicates structural misunderstanding of the methodology.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Improve phase standard content

items.Criterion: The quick wins recommended are distinct from the long-term 90-day action plan items.
items.Rationale: The prompt distinguishes immediate quick wins from the structured 90-day plan; a report that lists the same items in both sections does not reflect the intended two-tier improvement approach.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'recommend 3 to 5 quick wins for immediate action and detail a 90-day action plan'

items.Criterion: Each quick win is described with sufficient specificity to be actionable (naming the process area, action, or metric to be affected).
items.Rationale: Quick wins that are vague (generic statements like 'improve quality') cannot serve as actionable guidance. Professional industrial engineering reports require specificity.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: manufacturing action plan specificity standards

items.Criterion: The 90-day action plan milestones are distributed across at least two distinct time intervals within the 90-day window.
items.Rationale: A single milestone at day 90 does not constitute a useful action plan; professional 90-day plans phase milestones across the timeline to allow progress tracking.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: 90-day action plan structuring

items.Criterion: The estimated scrap reductions attributed to recommendations are internally consistent (individual root cause reductions do not sum to more than the total 40% baseline defect rate).
items.Rationale: If individual root cause savings exceed the total defect baseline, the estimates are arithmetically invalid. A credible industrial engineering report must maintain this consistency.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: '40% defect/scrap rate'; 'estimated scrap reduction'

items.Criterion: The total estimated scrap reduction from all recommended actions is projected to meet or exceed the 20% reduction target.
items.Rationale: The goal is a 20% defect reduction. A credible action plan must demonstrate that the proposed actions are sufficient to reach the stated target.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'reduce by 20% over the next quarter'

items.Criterion: The Control phase includes at least one mechanism for monitoring defect rates after implementation (such as control charts, regular audits, or SPC).
items.Rationale: DMAIC Control phase must define a monitoring system to sustain gains. Omitting this makes the plan incomplete as a DMAIC deliverable.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Control phase standard content

items.Criterion: The Control phase defines what will trigger escalation or re-analysis if defect rates do not improve.
items.Rationale: A complete DMAIC Control plan must specify response plans for when the process deviates from targets, not only monitoring mechanisms.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Control response plan

items.Criterion: The annotated process flow map PNG includes visible annotations or markings indicating where improvements are recommended.
items.Rationale: The prompt requires the process flow map to be annotated with recommendations; a plain, unmodified flowchart does not satisfy this requirement.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Annotate the process flow map (found in defect_log_3months.xlsx) with recommendations'

items.Criterion: The annotations on the process flow map PNG correspond to actions or root causes discussed in the DMAIC report.
items.Rationale: The annotated flow map and the DMAIC report must be consistent; annotations that reference items absent from the report indicate a disconnect between artifacts.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Annotate the process flow map ... with recommendations'; multi-artifact tie-out requirement

items.Criterion: The Pareto chart PNG (if provided) reflects the defect categories analyzed in the DMAIC report.
items.Rationale: If updated Pareto charts are provided, they must be consistent with the defect analysis presented in the DMAIC report. Mismatched categories indicate inconsistency between artifacts.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'update the pareto charts if needed'

items.Criterion: The X-ray image finding (from XRY-01_PCB-E_U5.png) is referenced or discussed in the DMAIC report.
items.Rationale: The prompt provides the X-ray image as one of the three inputs to be used; failure to incorporate X-ray findings means the analysis is incomplete.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'an image from Xray XRY-01_PCB-E_U5.png'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report references findings derived from the defect log as a basis for root cause analysis or recommendations.
items.Rationale: The defect_log_3months.xlsx is a primary input; any DMAIC analysis that does not draw from the defect log is not data-backed as required.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'defect_log_3months.xlsx'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report references findings from the Pareto analysis as a basis for root cause prioritization.
items.Rationale: The 3mos_pareto.pptx is a primary input; a DMAIC report that ignores the Pareto analysis is not using all provided data as required.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'pareto analysis of the previous 3 months in a file called 3mos_pareto.pptx'

items.Criterion: The root causes identified are plausible for PCB or electronics assembly manufacturing (such as solder defects, component misplacement, process parameter drift, or material quality issues).
items.Rationale: Domain-appropriate root causes are required for an electronics manufacturing context; generic or non-manufacturing causes indicate insufficient domain knowledge.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'electronics manufacturing assembly plant'

items.Criterion: The quick wins identified are realistically achievable within a timeframe shorter than 90 days.
items.Rationale: Quick wins by definition are immediate actions distinguishable from the 90-day plan; recommending actions that require months of preparation as quick wins is logically inconsistent.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'quick wins for immediate action'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report quantifies the current defect period as 3 months.
items.Rationale: The prompt specifies the analysis covers 3 months of defect history; the report must reflect this timeframe to correctly frame the problem scope.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'the past 3 months'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report does not recommend actions that contradict the data presented in the Analyze phase.
items.Rationale: Internal consistency requires that improvement actions in the Improve phase address the root causes identified in the Analyze phase; recommending unrelated actions undermines the DMAIC logic chain.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC internal consistency requirement

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report does not contain placeholder text such as TBD, TODO, or INSERT DATA HERE.
items.Rationale: Placeholder text indicates an incomplete deliverable that would be professionally unusable as an action plan submission to a manager.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: professional deliverable completeness standard

items.Criterion: The annotated process flow map is visually readable with process steps distinguishable from annotation markers.
items.Rationale: An annotated process flow map in which annotations obscure the original process steps is unusable as an engineering communication tool.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: engineering diagram readability standards

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report includes a summary table or structured list for the 90-day action plan rather than presenting it in unstructured prose only.
items.Rationale: A 90-day action plan with owners, milestones, resources, and acceptance criteria requires a structured format to be useful and scannable; prose paragraphs make cross-referencing owners to milestones impractical.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: action plan formatting standard

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report uses section headers that clearly identify each phase of the DMAIC framework.
items.Rationale: A DMAIC report without clearly labeled phase headers does not allow a reader to navigate the document or verify that all phases are addressed.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC report formatting standard

items.Criterion: The implementation cost or resource estimates in the DMAIC report are differentiated by action item rather than presented as a single aggregate figure.
items.Rationale: Action-level cost estimates allow prioritization and budget planning; a single aggregate figure does not support owner-level resource planning required by the action plan structure.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'implementation cost or resource estimate'

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report does not state that the defect reduction target will be achieved without providing supporting data or estimates.
items.Rationale: Asserting goal achievement without quantitative backing violates the data-backed requirement; this failure mode is distinct from the positive criterion requiring supporting estimates.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'Recommendations must be data-backed'

items.Criterion: The acceptance criteria in the 90-day action plan are measurable (include numeric thresholds, defect rates, or testable conditions) rather than subjective statements.
items.Rationale: Acceptance criteria that cannot be objectively verified (such as 'improve quality significantly') cannot function as completion gates in a professional action plan.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: acceptance criteria standards for manufacturing action plans

items.Criterion: The Measure phase includes at least one quantitative metric beyond the overall defect rate (such as defects per unit, defect rate by product type, or defect rate by process step).
items.Rationale: DMAIC Measure phase must disaggregate the defect metric to enable root cause analysis; reporting only the 40% aggregate rate does not provide the granularity needed for the Analyze phase.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Measure phase disaggregation requirement

items.Criterion: The DMAIC report's Improve or Control phase addresses how the gains will be sustained after the 90-day plan concludes.
items.Rationale: Sustainability is a core DMAIC Control phase requirement; a report that addresses only initial implementation without a sustainability mechanism is incomplete.
items.Citation: Domain knowledge: DMAIC Control phase sustainability requirement

items.Criterion: The three delivered artifacts (DMAIC PDF report, annotated process flow map PNG, and Pareto chart PNG) are all present in the response.
items.Rationale: The prompt requires all three artifact types; a response missing any one of them is incomplete.
items.Citation: TASK_PROMPT: 'pdf output', 'annotated process flow map as a png', 'updated pareto charts ... in png format'
